thread:
Cam: noticed a retry cascade during yesterday's traffic spike — a bunch of short streaming calls retried and ended up saturating the ingress queue. logs attached but TL;DR: retries + soft hedging caused head-of-line queuing and then downstream 503s.
Tia: ugh. do we have per-route retry budgets right now? or is it global?
Cam: global budget today. per-tenant throttles exist but not per-route. also streaming requests keep connections open so queue time balloons.
Ben: idea: add a 'streaming-retry-window' that disables automatic hedging for live streams > N seconds and instead uses long-tail-prefetch/backoff. avoids duplicate concurrent streams.
Jun: big Q: how do we detect "streaming" cheaply at the gateway? content-type? KEEPALIVE frames?
Omar: we can mark on upgrade/handshake. when client opens streaming session we set header `x-rw-streaming: 1`. cheap and explicit. clients/SDKs opt-in.
Tia: that helps, but we still need fail-safes when clients don't opt-in. maybe fallback if response has `transfer-encoding: chunked` and first chunk after >500ms -> mark streaming.
Ben: agree on opt-in + heuristic. next, the retry policy: per-route token bucket for retry attempts. token refill tied to successful completions instead of time, to avoid refilling during failing surge.
Cam: can you sketch a sample config? I'm worried about PR complexity.
Omar: here's a draft snippet we discussed:
```yaml
route: /generate
retry_policy:
  max_attempts: 3
  per_route_budget: 50 # tokens
  refill_on_success: true
  streaming_behavior:
    hedging: false
    backpressure_threshold_ms: 250
    opt_in_header: x-rw-streaming
```
Ben: nice. also add `reject_non_idempotent_when_degraded: true` so we early-reject risky retries for POST-like ops.
Tia: for telemetry, surface `retry_budget_remaining` and `streaming_flag` on traces. that will help SLO debugging.
ops-bot: incident: edge-ingress-queue-saturation at 2025-09-14T18:42:12Z (auto-detected). alert routed to #eng-sre.
Jun: on graceful degradation: if per-route budget exhausted, should we 429 or 202 (accept async)? 429 is clearer but many clients don't have async paths.
Cam: prefer 429 + retry-after header. for SDKs we can plumb a fallback `enqueue_for_processing` that returns 202 for supported clients.
Omar: implementation plan suggestion:
- opt-in header for streaming (SDK change)
- heuristic mark for legacy clients
- per-route token bucket with refill-on-success
- disallow hedging for marked-streaming routes
- trace metrics + dashboard
Tia: assignable tasks? I can own the dashboard + telemetry.
Ben: I'll prototype the token-bucket logic in the gateway (golang). Jun can spec client-side SDK change.
Jun: will do SDK opt-in + doc PR.
Cam: cool. can we aim for a small canary next week? low-risk flag.
Tia: +1. will add experiment flag `edge.retry_cascade_mitigation` and a canary rollout plan.
Omar: I'll draft the RFC with config API and failure modes.
Cam: thanks all. I'll post logs/grafana links in the thread and ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
